text:
vince: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Two asks from the field: (1) how do we explain the value of "serving-first" in one sentence to a skeptical CTO, and (2) what are the three things we never compromise on when negotiating enterprise deals?

tara: One-liner idea: 'We make LLM features predictable: lower cost per token, reliable latency at scale, and safe rollouts.' Keeps it outcome-focused.

leo: For enterprise negotiables: we shouldn't compromise on data isolation (customer KMS + audit), SLO-backed latency guarantees for paid tiers, and clear rollback/fallback policies. Other stuff (pricing flexibility, onboarding support) is negotiable.

priya: Field note: CTOS push back when vendors talk about models. They care about total cost and operational risk. If we lead with model names, we lose. We should include a short ROI calc in one-pagers: tokens/day x baseline vs Redwood optimized.

hanna: Related: can marketing create two versions of collateral? (1) a technical brief for infra/eng buyers with p50/p95/p99 benches and (2) an executive brief for CTOs with ROI and risk reduction bullets.

product-bot: Action created: "marketing/briefs/serving-first-cta" assigned to @hanna, due in 5 business days.

vince: Great. Leadership Q: are we open to bundling partner training or MLOps integrations as paid add-ons, or do we keep partnerships loose (referrals only)? This affects the sales playbook.

tara: We can offer certified partner integrations (paid) and keep deep training/labeling as partner-led services. We don't want to build a training stack, but we can monetize partner-enabled solutions and provide a managed-services SKU.

leo: Competitor angle: some rivals advertise large model catalogs and claim that's the moat. Our counter: emphasize migration velocity and predictable economics. We should prepare two rebuttal lines for sales: one for price-sensitive buyers, one for reliability-first buyers.

priya: Sales request: what signal thresholds trigger a proactive outreach for Dedicated? Suggestion: sustained 30-day token growth > 3x, monthly spend > $10k, or security/regulatory tag set in account. Can leadership confirm?

vince: That sounds reasonable. We'll formalize thresholds and include them in the Growth Kit. Also: let's add a short checklist for "when to recommend Private": regulated workloads, on-prem requirement, or mandatory customer-managed KMS.

hanna: Small ask: can leadership give a short approved line about where we sit vs cloud hyperscalers? Helps with RFP answers.

tara: Approved line draft: 'Unlike cloud GPU providers, Redwood offers an opinionated serving platform that guarantees predictable latency and cost for inference workloads while enabling customers to migrate models and infrastructure with minimal app changes.'

vince: Perfect. Thanks. One final operational ask: can we publish an anonymized case study that shows a real customer's latency SLO improvements + cost delta? Sales needs it.

product-bot: Note: case study ingestion policy requires legal sign-off and customer anonymization. Product will start intake with two candidate customers this week.

vince: Excellent. Appreciate the quick clarifications. :raised_hands:
